premises.text: Existing recommendation systems rely on reviews from strangers, which is not natural.
premises.evidence_span: all of these systems are dependent on giving you reviews and recommendations from strangers.

premises.text: Current systems provide average ratings, failing to personalize recommendations.
premises.evidence_span: all of these systems simply give you the average rating for all reviews, despite your unique personal taste.

premises.text: Fake reviews are a prevalent issue in online recommendations.
premises.evidence_span: one-third of reviews online are fake.

premises.text: High-quality reviews from trusted sources can improve recommendations.
premises.evidence_span: give you access to high-quality reviews from trusted sources.

premises.text: The algorithm can match users with others who have similar tastes.
premises.evidence_span: LiveStar algorithmically measures your taste and then compares it to other people.

premises.text: LiveStar saves users time by aggregating reviews quickly.
premises.evidence_span: Imagine how much time it would take to go online, read all of these critic reviews, aggregate these opinions by hand, and compare them.

premises.text: The Q&A feature facilitates easy recommendations from friends.
premises.evidence_span: LiveStar has a Q&A feature that lets me send a question, a request for some recommendations to friends.

premises.text: LiveStar provides recommendations across various categories.
premises.evidence_span: you can go to LiveStar for restaurants, what to eat, when you're at the restaurant, what music to listen to, and what movie to watch.

value.text: Users receive personalized and trustworthy recommendations quickly.
value.evidence_span: it's fast, it's simple, and it's easy to begin on.

notes: No separate premises for the various recommendation sources as they all contribute to the same solution.
